items.title: Rethinking Flood Protection Through a ‘No-Regret’ Lens
items.author: eugenetan95
items.description: Governments in our region and beyond must plan today for tomorrow's floods, in a warming world. Regret can be minimised, if not eliminated.

items.title: The “Karenni Model”: Wartime Governance in Contested Territory
items.author: eugenetan95
items.description: The Karenni governance experience in Myanmar explains how wartime governance emerges and is sustained under intensified conflict, fragmented political orders, and uneven international engagement. But this requires continued efforts to maintain minimum levels of territorial security and de-escalate conflict.

items.title: Malaysia’s Chinese Investment Boom Has a Hiring Problem
items.author: yeosiewhan
items.description: Chinese firms are investing in Malaysia at record levels, but many recent entrants tend to fill key technical and managerial positions with costly expatriates rather than develop Malaysian successors.

items.title: Indonesia’s Green Industrialisation Plans Have a Brown Problem
items.author: eugenetan95
items.description: Indonesia has managed to surpass targets for renewable energy. The problem, however, is that green sources of energy continue to exist with their brown counterparts.

items.title: How Do ASEAN Countries Fare in Managing Global Economic Shocks?
items.author: izaridati
items.description: Geopolitical conflict, energy disruptions and shifting global supply chains are testing Southeast Asia’s economic resilience. ASEANFocus+ asked regional experts how individual countries are responding and whether ASEAN has the tools to collectively manage the next shock. Their insights highlight the different challenges facing the region, as well as the need for stronger regional coordination, deeper market integration and greater resilience across energy, trade, food and financial systems.

items.title: The Humanitarian Costs of Starlink’s Policy
items.author: eugenetan95
items.description: Starlink is seeking to curtail access to one of its Internet services. This would affect many conflict-afflicted regions in Myanmar

items.title: China’s Drive for Food Self-Sufficiency: What It Means for ASEAN Countries
items.author: eugenetan95
items.description: China is determined to become more self-sufficient in its food supply. This will have implications for ASEAN economies.

items.title: Prabowo and Indonesia’s Ulema Council: Is MUI Losing Traction Again?
items.author: eugenetan95
items.description: President Prabowo was absent from a key Ulema Council of Indonesia (MUI) event last month. This signals that the organisation might now rank lower on his list of priorities.

items.title: Why Indonesia Needs a China Strategy Now
items.author: eugenetan95
items.description: The authors argue that Indonesia needs a more coherent strategy for its relationship with China.

items.title: Gig Workers in Malaysia: Is the New Law a Good Deal?
items.author: eugenetan95
items.description: Malaysia’s Gig Workers Act, which took effect in April 2026, is a legislative milestone for the Madani administration. Malaysia’s 1.64 million gig workers stand to gain from the introduction of contractual frameworks, mandatory injury insurance, dispute settlement mechanisms, and a consultative council for setting minimum earnings. However, various policy gaps still need to be addressed.

items.title: Should Malaysia Become a Global Education Hub?
items.author: yeosiewhan
items.description: Malaysia is setting its sights on becoming a global education hub. In doing so, however, it might have overlooked its edge as a regional education hub.

items.title: Calibrating the Singapore-US Security Anchor for a New Era: An American View
items.author: chahaewon
items.description: As the US moves into a more transactional mode, Singapore’s standing as a capable and self-reliant partner will put it in good stead.

items.title: Nahdlatul Ulama’s Establishment Versus Grassroots Leadership Race Will Affect Its Political Alignments
items.author: yeosiewhan
items.description: The leadership contest in Nahdlatul Ulama is consequential. The next executive chairman could stay the course and remain close to the President, or respond to grassroots calls for change.

items.title: From Streamlining to Delivery: Vietnam’s Second Administrative Test
items.author: yeosiewhan
items.description: Vietnam’s Central Committee has embarked on the most sweeping administrative overhaul in decades. But success is likely to be uneven.

items.title: Different Sectors, Same Direction: Indonesia’s Quiet Recentralisation
items.author: chahaewon
items.description: Indonesia’s revised financial omnibus law reflects a broader trend towards executive recentralisation, renewing concerns over institutional independence and accountability.

items.title: Parti Wawasan Negara’s Gambit: A Bridge Too Far
items.author: chahaewon
items.description: Parti Wawasan Negara is styling itself as a “bridge” from Parti Islam SeMalaysia and the United Malays National Organisation. The odds of Wawasan attaining this role are long.

items.title: Why PAS Wants to Avoid Going Solo
items.author: chahaewon
items.description: Parti Islam SeMalaysia is unlikely to fly solo as it prepares for the upcoming 16th General Election in Malaysia.

items.title: Bangsa Johor’s Resounding Vote
items.author: yeosiewhan
items.description: The recent Johor state polls have some bearing on the upcoming general elections. But to many Johoreans, the polls were more about the pride of being part of the rich southern state.

items.title: ASEAN and Canada: Building Bridges with the Great White North
items.author: chahaewon
items.description: Canada can improve its relevance to ASEAN by focusing on areas such as food security and energy transition.
